verse.text: “You are worthy, our Lord and God, to receive glory and honor and power, for you created all things, and by your will they were created and have their being.”

reflection.scripture: “You are worthy, our Lord and God, to receive glory and honor and power, for you created all things, and by your will they were created and have their being.”
reflection.observation: This verse captures the heart of heavenly worship — the twenty-four elders fall before the throne and declare God's worthiness to receive glory, honor, and power. The reason? Creation itself. Every mountain, ocean, star, and breath exists because God willed it. This isn't passive acknowledgment; it's active, surrendered worship that recognizes God as both Creator and Sustainer. The phrase 'by your will they were created and have their being' reminds us that existence itself is a gift, not a given.
reflection.application: In a world that often feels chaotic and self-directed, this verse invites us to pause and remember: we exist on purpose. Our lives, our struggles, our joys — all held together by God's will. Today, let that truth shape your perspective. When anxiety rises, when plans unravel, when you feel unseen, return to this: the same God who spoke galaxies into being holds your life with intention. Let worship be your response, not just in song, but in surrender.
reflection.prayer: Lord, You are worthy of all glory, honor, and power. Thank You that my life is not an accident — You created me, and by Your will I have my being. When I feel overwhelmed by the noise of this world, draw my heart back to this truth. Let my life be an act of worship today, surrendered to the One who holds all things together. In Jesus' name, Amen.
